title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance (Canonical Guidelines + ADRs)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
=======
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding, infrastructure (IaC), model-serving, observability, and performance. It also enumerates active ADRs (architecture decision records) that govern cross-team trade-offs. The purpose is to provide single-source guidance for engineering teams building production inference services and integrations.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all backend services, serving runtime components, control plane, client-facing APIs, internal infra IaC, and observability instrumentation. Does NOT replace team-level runbooks for emergency operations.

Owners and governance
---------------------
- Document owner: Architecture Council (chair: Aisha Patel)
- Primary responsible teams: eng-serving-runtime, eng-infra, eng-platform, eng-sre
- Review cadence: quarterly; ADRs reviewed during architecture review board monthly meeting

Quick links
-----------
- API Standards (section) — this file
- ADR index: see the ADR section below
- Related runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks

1) API Standards
----------------
Goal: Provide stable, discoverable, and versioned APIs that minimize breakage for downstream customers while enabling iterative improvements.

Principles
- Backwards compatibility by default. Use additive changes where possible.
- Version explicitly for breaking changes (semantic versioning at the API surface: v1, v2).
- Strongly-typed request/response contracts and machine-readable schemas (OpenAPI 3.1).
- Authentication via OAuth2 bearer tokens (internal service tokens: mTLS where required).

Design rules
- Spec and docs: every public/internal API MUST have an OpenAPI 3.1 spec checked into the service repo under /api/openapi.yaml and published to the API catalog.
- URLs: use nouns, hyphenated-lowercase, and plural resources. Example: /v1/models/{model_id}/infer
- Methods: use GET for safe reads, POST for commands/creates, PATCH for partial updates. Avoid overloading verbs.
- Pagination: cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Include total_count only when inexpensive to compute.
- Rate limiting headers: include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset on responses for public endpoints.

Error handling
- Use problem+json (RFC 7807) for structured errors.
- Standard error fields: {"type","title","status","detail","instance","error_code"}.
- Error codes: use short namespaced codes (e.g., model.not_found, request.invalid_payload). Document codes in the OpenAPI spec.

Backward-compatibility policy
- Non-breaking changes: documented and can be deployed without version bump.
- Breaking changes: must be proposed as an ADR and coordinated with API consumers; provide a deprecation window of >= 90 days for public APIs.

2) Coding Standards and SDLC
----------------------------
Languages in primary use: Go (runtime, infra agents), Python (evals, tooling), TypeScript (console/backend), Terraform/HCL (IaC).

General rules
- Follow language-specific style guides (gofmt/goimports for Go; black/isort/flake8 for Python; eslint/prettier for TS).
- Enforce static analysis in CI with mandatory passing checks before merge.
- Unit test coverage: target >= 60% for non-trivial business logic; critical runtime paths >= 80%.
- PR size: aim for < 400 lines changed; PRs > 800 lines require lead approval.
- Commit messages: Conventional Commits preferred (type(scope): summary).

Dependencies and secrets
- Dependabot or equivalent automated tooling for dependency updates.
- Secrets must be stored in the team vault (AWS Secrets Manager / HashiCorp Vault) and never checked into source. Use environment injection patterns.

3) Infrastructure (IaC) Standards
--------------------------------
- All cloud infra MUST be managed via Terraform (module registry under terraform/).
- Environments: dev, staging, prod. Use separate cloud accounts or VPCs per environment.
- Networking: follow the standard VPC layout (public/private subnets, NAT, VPC endpoints for service-to-service egress).
- Naming conventions: resource names must include environment, team, and purpose. Example: rdx-prod-serving-gpu-01
- Change management: any production terraform apply that changes networking/security groups requires an infra review and 48-hour lead time for scheduled maintenance.

Security controls
- IAM: least privilege by default; use role-based access and temporary credentials.
- KMS: customer and platform keys must be in KMS; HSM for keys in private deployments where required.
- Image scanning: container images scanned in CI; critical vulnerabilities (CVSS >= 7.0) must be triaged within 72 hours.

4) Model-Serving Standards
--------------------------
Scope: serving runtime, model packaging, quantization, caching, batching, rollouts.

Model packaging and registry
- Every model served in production must be stored in the model registry with metadata: model_id, version, architecture, quantization_profile, tokenizer_version, reproducible_hash, owners, evaluation_summary.
- Use standard container artifact or OCI layout for model bundles. Include a manifest.json that follows the model registry schema.

Quantization & profiles
- Supported quantization profiles: fp16, int8 (symmetric), awq/q4f_fast (team-supported). Each profile MUST have a performance and quality benchmark entry in the registry.
- Quantization decisions are driven by workload-specific evals. See /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles.

Inference runtime behaviors
- Batching: enable continuous batching for high-throughput routes; fall back to single-request paths for low-latency SLO routes.
- KV-cache: runtime must expose optional per-route prefix caching; cache keys include model_id, model_version, prompt_prefix_hash.
- Beam/decoding defaults: streaming with top_p/top_k settings exposed per-route; default deterministic seed for evals.

Rollouts and compatibility
- Canary policy: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over configurable intervals with automated quality gates (latency and regression tests).
- Fallbacks: every model variant must declare compatible fallback variants (smaller model, quantized variant) to be used when capacity is constrained.

5) Observability Standards
--------------------------
Metrics
- Use Prometheus for metrics, structured with the following convention: <service>_<subsystem>_<metric>_total/gauge/histogram. Label cardinality must be controlled (max 10k series per metric).
- Required metrics for services: request_count, request_errors_total (with error_code label), request_duration_seconds (histogram), in_flight_requests, model_cache_hit_ratio.

Logging
- JSON structured logs with keys: timestamp, level, service, trace_id, span_id, request_id, user_id (if applicable), message, fields.
- Log retention: infra logs 90 days; audit logs 365 days (configurable per customer).

Tracing
- Distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry. Trace context must be propagated across RPCs and worker queues.
- Sample rate: platform default 1% (adjustable per service under eng-sre guidance); critical paths increase to 10% for debug windows.

SLOs and alerting
- SLOs must be declared in the service README and registered in the central SLO dashboard. Minimum SLOs for customer-facing inference: 99.9% availability/month. Example latency SLOs: 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 250ms for small-model (<2B) hosted routes; 95th <= 1s for large-context or large-model routes.
- Error budget burn policies: automated paging for sustained error budget burn > 5% in a rolling 24h window.

6) Performance Standards and Benchmarks
-------------------------------------
- Benchmark harness: every model and runtime change that affects execution path must include performance benchmarks in CI (latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization).
- Benchmark environment: use standardized instance types (e.g., A100-80GB for large-model baseline, A10G for mid-range) and fixed sequence lengths for comparable results.
- Target per-token cost reduction goals: teams should track tokens/dollar and aim for 15% year-over-year improvements through batching, caching, and kernel optimizations.

Benchmarking procedure (short)
1. Deploy model variant to the isolated perf cluster (tag: perf-YYYYMMDD).
2. Run synthetic load with representative prompt distribution (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).
3. Collect latency, throughput, GPU/memory metrics, and compare against baseline thresholds.
4. If regression > 5% in p95 latency or >10% throughput drop, open a regression triage ticket and halt rollout.

7) ADRs (Selected and Active)
----------------------------
This section summarizes key architecture decisions with links to the full ADR. Teams must consult full ADR documents for rationale and migration steps.

- ADR-2025-08: Runtime kernel selection strategy — decided to use hybrid kernel selector (heuristic + ML-based ranking) for per-model/per-sequence optimizations. (link: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/architecture-standards-kernel-adr-2025-08)
- ADR-2025-11: API versioning policy — semantic versioning at API surface, adopt OpenAPI 3.1 as canonical spec format.
- ADR-2026-01: Default quantization profile — adopt int8-symmetric for throughput-first routes with documented quality budgets.
- ADR-2026-03: Observability backend — adopt Prometheus + Loki + Tempo (OpenTelemetry) as the platform stack.

For each ADR the expected fields in the ADR are: status, context, decision, consequences, migration plan, owner.

8) Change / Exception process
-----------------------------
- Exceptions: any deviation from these standards must be filed as an RFC and approved by the Architecture Council. Keep exceptions timeboxed and documented in the related_pages list.
- Emergency changes: document and file a postmortem within 7 days.

9) Templates and Examples (appendix)
-----------------------------------
- OpenAPI example (snippet):
  POST /v1/models/{model_id}/infer
  Request schema: {"input": "string", "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0.0}
  Response schema: {"id": "string", "outputs": [{"text": "string","tokens": 42}], "model_version": "string"}

- Terraform module header example:
  module "serving_cluster" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@repo/terraform/serving-cluster.git//modules/cluster"
    env    = var.env
    owner  = "eng-serving-runtime"
  }

- Observability alert example:
  Alert: ServiceHighP95Latency
  Expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service, route)) > 0.5
  For: 5m
  Labels: severity=page
  Runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/service-high-p95-latency
